content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost break delay, a short 2-agent loan from general, and payments callback. It is predicted to hold 91.2% service level for 13:15-15:15 at zero extra cost.","why":"The FD special-rate email drove general calls 20–45% over forecast (new-offer enquiries 2.74x normal). Separately, payments is running about 4 agents short because of sick calls, and its service level fell to 25.2%. For the 13:15-15:15 window, P1 predicts 91.2% overall (payments 86.9%, general 96.1%) against an 80% target, with no policy breaches and no cost. Rest of day is predicted at 96.1%. Note that doing nothing (P0) is also predicted to reach the target at 91.0%, so P1 is a small, free safeguard rather than a rescue.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) is also free and predicted at 91.0% with a slightly lower abandon rate (2.2% vs 2.5%). P1 adds only 0.2 points, but it actively supports the short-staffed payments queue.","P2 is the strongest option: 92.6% overall, payments 88.1%, and the lowest abandon rate at 1.9%. It costs ₹444 and adds chat deflection, which leaves general untouched.","P3 spends ₹360, the last of the overtime budget, yet is predicted slightly worse at 90.8%. It is not worth it.","Moving 2 agents from general carries some risk while campaign calls are still elevated. General is still predicted at 96.1%, so the risk looks small."],"watch":"Watch general volume during the 13:15-14:00 loan. If campaign calls spike again, return the 2 agents early. If payments service level is not recovering toward ~87% by 14:00, consider switching to P2 (₹444)."}
